Host > Rec Sound / Stop / Capture Screen.

The original hands both jobs to its OSD (EMU::start_record_sound, EMU::capture_screen), which on Win32 taps DirectSound and the D2D back buffer. This port's OSD has neither - those methods are empty (src/core/sdl/osd_sound.cpp, osd_screen.cpp) and the core is not to be modified - so both are done here instead, from data the host already holds:

  • the recording is written from the very buffer the SDL audio callback hands to the sound device, so what lands in the file is exactly what was played, and
  • the screenshot is written from the same framebuffer the renderer uploads, so it is the guest's own 640x400 picture with no status bar, scaling or filtering applied.

Threading: feedSound runs on SDL's audio thread while everything else runs on the main thread. The caller must hold the audio device lock (SDL_LockAudioDevice) across startSoundRecording / stopSoundRecording so the file cannot be closed out from under a write in progress.

proc feedSound(samples: pointer; frames: int) {....raises: [IOError],
    tags: [WriteIOEffect], forbids: [].}
Appends frames interleaved stereo int16 frames. Called from SDL's audio thread: no allocation, no exceptions, and a short write simply stops the recording rather than trying to recover. 
proc isSoundRecording(): bool {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
proc saveScreenshot(framebuffer: ptr UncheckedArray[uint32]; width, height: int): string {.
    ...raises: [], tags: [ReadEnvEffect, ReadIOEffect, TimeEffect, WriteDirEffect,
                       ReadDirEffect, WriteIOEffect], forbids: [].}
Writes one PNG of the guest's screen and returns its path, or "" if it could not be written. framebuffer is the core's ARGB8888 buffer, top-down, with width pixels per row. 
proc startSoundRecording(rate: int): string {....raises: [IOError], tags: [
    ReadEnvEffect, ReadIOEffect, WriteDirEffect, ReadDirEffect, TimeEffect,
    WriteIOEffect], forbids: [].}
Begins a new recording and returns the file it writes to, or "" if the file could not be created (a full or unwritable Music folder - the one failure a user can actually hit). Recording while already recording is a no-op that returns "". 
proc stopSoundRecording(rate: int) {....raises: [], tags: [WriteIOEffect],
                                     forbids: [].}
Rewrites the two length fields the header could not know up front, then closes the file. A recorder that already died on a write error is simply already closed.
